text:
Predicates:
CanRegisterVote(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateElection2024(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir(x) ::: x is Vladimir.
Ekaterina(x) ::: x is Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegisterVote(x) → ParticipateElection2024(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 election.
CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegisterVote(x) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote.
CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: A person either has US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir does not hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(RussianOfficial(Vladimir) ∧ HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir)) ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official who holds Taiwanese citizenship.
EkaterinaCanRegister(x) ∨ RussianOfficial(x) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote or she is a Russian official.
Premises for the conclusion:
¬(CanRegisterVote(Ekaterina) ∧ ParticipateElection2024(Vladimir)) ::: It is not true that Ekaterina can register to vote and Vladimir can participate in the election.
Conclusion:
¬(CanRegisterVote(Ekaterina) ∧ ParticipateElection2024(Vladimir)) ::: It is not true that Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States and Vladimir can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
